TEKKEN 7 Quick Impressions

TEKKEN 7 is a fighting game from 2017. I played for about 2 hours and a few matches so here are my thoughts.

Combat feels good. It is fast, hits feel strong and there is clear depth. Even without full knowledge of mechanics it is still fun. But you can tell the game needs time to really learn.

I tried characters like Kazuya Mishima and Jin Kazama. They feel different which is nice but also makes it harder for new players.

Gamepad controls are ok but not perfect. Inputs sometimes feel a bit off if you are not used to Tekken.

Graphics are fine but outdated. Some effects still look cool but overall it feels old.

I did not play story so this is only about gameplay and a few matches. Online works fine nothing special.

Important point TEKKEN 7 was a very good game at release and stayed strong until around 2023. But in 2026 there are better options. Fighting games improved a lot.

So now I would recommend newer fighting games or the latest Tekken instead. TEKKEN 7 is still good but not the best choice today.

Verdict
Good core but outdated in 2026. Worth it only on sale or if you are curious.

Tekken 7 is an outstanding fighting game that delivers everything you could want from the genre. The combat is smooth, responsive, and incredibly satisfying, with a huge roster of unique characters, each offering their own fighting style and techniques. Whether you're playing casually with friends or learning advanced combos, every match feels exciting and rewarding.

The graphics and animations are excellent, and the special moves and Rage Arts make every fight feel cinematic. The game offers plenty of content, including online battles, arcade mode, treasure battles, and character customization, giving you countless hours of entertainment.

What makes Tekken 7 truly special is its depth. It's easy to pick up but takes real skill to master, making every victory feel earned. The online matches are intense, and there's always something new to learn.

If you're a fan of fighting games or want to experience one of the best competitive fighters ever created, Tekken 7 is an absolute must-play. It has amazing gameplay, fantastic replay value, and remains one of my favorite fighting games of all time. Highly recommended!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the story mode is thin and short.

citations.review_text:
Tekken 7 is the fighting game that saved the franchise. After years of wandering in the wilderness (Tekken 6 was a mess, Tag 2 was bloated), Namco made a game that understood what made Tekken work: fast-paced, frame-data-dependent gameplay where positioning and timing matter more than mashing buttons. With 91% positive reviews across 95,000 Steam users, the community has spoken: this is legitimately great.

The roster is massive and diverse — each character feels genuinely different, with movesets that require actual study to master. The Rage Art and Rage Drive mechanics add flashy momentum shifts without breaking the game's fundamentals. The visuals are stunning even now, with gorgeous stage design and character models that hold up. The story mode is thin (forgettable melodrama about the Mishima clan), but the core fighting is tight — responsive, balanced, and rewarding for players who put in the work to learn combos and frame data.

The PC port is solid. The competitive scene thrived around this game for years. Casual players can mash and have fun; serious players can grind frame data and theory-craft for hundreds of hours. The character variety means there's a playstyle for everyone.

Criticisms: single-player content is sparse (story's short, arcade modes are basic), the DLC roster is bloated (19 characters as DLC feels excessive), and by 2026 standards the online population has thinned. Tekken 8 launched in 2024 and split the community, so T7's player count has cratered. But the 354 concurrent players still finding matches speaks to how good the core game is.

At its price (often under $10 on sale), this is an absolute steal for anyone interested in fighting games. It's the Tekken entry that recaptured the magic and proved the franchise wasn't dead — just needed to remember what made it great.

Essential for fighting game fans.

This is the first Tekken episode available on PC. Making its debut, Tekken 7 is a solid fighting game with an incredible initial roster that covers most fighting lovers' needs. The gameplay is the strongest point of the production, adding some interesting features like movement shortcuts and the "Rage Art"—a powerful but blockable super move that can be used by pressing just one button when our energy is very low. The story mode is not bad, chronicling the saga of the Mishima family. Characters are highly customizable, allowing us to change their appearance as we like. The graphics are based on Unreal Engine 4, making the game visually rewarding.
Bandai Namco also made some unfortunate choices that reduced the quality of the experience: the time attack, survival, and team battle modes have been removed. Many historical characters are only available through DLCs and lack any story content; ending sequences are limited to just 28 characters, and most of them are short and comedic. Even Tekken Bowl must be purchased separately. The soundtrack is overall okay, with two or three tracks worth mentioning, but it is nothing comparable to what we had in the first five Tekken episodes or in Tekken Tag.
The core gameplay still rocks; what's around it could have been better.

My score: 8.0

I'm just a casual fighting game player who's been playing the Tekken series since Tekken 5, so this review comes from that perspective.

As for the story, I think it's pretty good. While it's not the strongest aspect of the game, it does a satisfying job of wrapping up the long-running Mishima family conflict. And, as always, it wouldn't be a Tekken game without someone throwing a family member off a cliff.

The character roster is excellent and offers a great variety of fighters, especially with the addition of several guest characters through collaborations. As for the original Tekken cast, I really like their updated designs. Ling Xiaoyu, in particular, looks significantly different compared to the previous games, and I think her redesign is one of the best in the series.

The gameplay introduces new mechanics such as Rage Art and Rage Drive, adding another layer of strategy to every match. Both mechanics can completely turn the tide of a fight when used at the right moment. On top of that, combos feel much smoother than in previous entries, especially when juggling opponents in the air, making the combat more satisfying and rewarding to learn.

As for the online mode, I haven't experienced any major issues so far. Matches have been smooth, and playing against other people has been a great way to improve my skills and learn different playstyles.

This game also holds a special place in my heart. Back in college, my friends and I spent countless hours playing Tekken 7 together. At the time, we could only play a pirated copy because we simply couldn't afford the original. Now, years later, I'm finally able to buy the game with money I earned from my own job. It feels incredibly rewarding to finally own and support a game that gave me so many unforgettable memories.

Overall, Tekken 7 is one of my favorite entries in the series. Whether you're a longtime fan or just a casual player like me, it offers an excellent roster, satisfying gameplay, and an exper…
